text:
Predicates:
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
HasBackbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
ReproducesByMating(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
QueenBee(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Premises:
∀x (Animal(x) → (Invertebrate(x) ⊕ Vertebrate(x))) ::: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates.
∀x (HasBackbone(x) → ReproducesByMating(x)) ::: All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Vertebrate(x) → HasBackbone(x)) ::: All vertebrate animals have a backbone.
∀x (Bee(x) → ¬ReproducesByMating(x)) ::: All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (QueenBee(x) → Bee(x)) ::: All queen bees are bees.
Bee(harry) ::: Harry is a bee.
Conclusion:
Invertebrate(harry) ∨ QueenBee(harry) ::: Harry is an invertebrate or a queen bee.
